clue.text: Said to be weighing down little devil first bursting in

indicators.note: first tells us the little devil's letters lead the answer

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil

indicators.note: said to be marks a sound-alike: the word for weighing down is spoken, then spelt differently

parts.note: loading something weighs it down

explanation.surface: Someone weighed down by a mischievous sprite is supposedly bursting into a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said to be' signals that LOADING (weighing down) is heard as LODING. 'First' puts IMP at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Collapsing violently inward is the sense of the verb here, the opposite of exploding outward.

clue.text: Cat called or cow lowed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver the sound of the cow's noise stands for the written letters

parts.note: a cow that lowed made a moo, so it mooed

explanation.surface: A farmyard question of whether the cat or the cow made the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' signals the sound-alike: MOOED (cow lowed) said aloud approximates the cat's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat calling out makes its characteristic miaow sound, the past tense of that cry.

clue.text: Left with an antelope or reptile

parts.note: the izard is a goat-antelope of the Pyrenees, a chamois

explanation.surface: A zoological choice between a hoofed animal and a cold-blooded one.
explanation.walkthrough: The IZARD is the Pyrenean chamois, a crossword favourite among antelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko or iguana is an example of this scaly, four-legged reptile.

clue.text: It's to do with skin that's tender, maltreated somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Skin that has been ill-treated is left sore to the touch.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition took in 'It's' and 'that's', which cannot replace an adjective; those are link words, and 'to do with skin' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the dermis, the layer of tissue under the epidermis, so concerning the body's covering.

clue.text: Scotsman getting up order inside for a girl

indicators.note: inside places the order's letters within the reversed name
getting up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A Scotsman rising to put things in order for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting up' turns IAN into NAI, and 'inside' puts OM (Order of Merit) within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical female name, Ruth's mother-in-law, so a name a woman might have.

clue.text: Murdered during the night at a guess

explanation.surface: A night-time killing reported tentatively.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a gunshot killing after dusk; figuratively a wild attempt made with no real knowledge.

clue.text: Vote in nearby pub?

parts.note: the pub round the corner is one's regular, and a vote is a choosing; read straight it means a ballot for a council

explanation.surface: A ballot held at the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A municipal ballot for council members of a district, the nearby seat of government.

clue.text: Film lightweight magician

explanation.surface: A movie about a feeble conjuror.
explanation.walkthrough: OZ is the abbreviation for ounce, a light weight, so the magician 'of OZ' is lightweight.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1939 musical movie with Judy Garland; its title figure is a sorcerer whose name carries the ounce abbreviation.

clue.text: A shade unwell

explanation.surface: Feeling slightly poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a hue slightly wrong, a shade can be 'off' a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint not quite matching, and slang for feeling slightly ill.

clue.text: Shut up corner of figure with nearly half a dozen sides

definitions.text: figure with nearly half a dozen sides

parts.note: pent means confined or shut up, as in pent-up
an angle is a corner

explanation.surface: Confining a corner of a shape that has almost six sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Nearly half a dozen is five: the figure is a five-pointed star.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star drawn with five straight lines, a five-sided figure in old usage.

clue.text: Was destined to have been entertained at a feast as reported

definitions.note: the definition is loose: (was) destined matches the participle

indicators.note: as reported points to a word heard, not seen, so the spoken form is spelt differently

parts.words: to have been entertained at a feast
parts.note: feted means honoured or entertained with a feast

explanation.surface: Someone was always going to be wined and dined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As reported' signals that FETED is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomed or predetermined by destiny is what this participle means.

clue.text: Picture one wise man

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a mage is a magus, a learned man

explanation.surface: A painting of one of the Magi.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness or representation, synonymous with a picture.

clue.text: A major person

parts.note: in law a major is someone who has come of age, not an army officer

explanation.surface: An important individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone over the age of majority, fully grown.

clue.text: Put on cast

explanation.surface: A costume was donned for the play.
explanation.walkthrough: To cast up a column of figures is an old way of saying to total it.
explanation.definitionFit: Attached or appended; and totalled, as in casting accounts.

clue.text: One in Paris before midweek had not tied the knot

definitions.note: an adjective here standing for a verb phrase: one who had not tied the knot is single

indicators.note: before puts the French number ahead of the day

parts.note: un is French for one
Wed, short for Wednesday, is the day in the middle of the week

explanation.surface: A Parisian who had not married by Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Single, never having married.

clue.text: It might be used by Spaniards to accentuate something

definitions.text: It might be used by Spaniards to accentuate something

parts.words: It might be used by Spaniards to accentuate something
parts.note: Spanish writing marks a letter with a wavy sign above it; read straight it suggests emphasis in speech

explanation.surface: Spaniards adding emphasis to something they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A wavy diacritic placed over an n in Spanish orthography.

clue.text: Rotter hurried back, in producing a rumour

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the rotter

parts.note: a cad is a rotter

indicators.note: back turns the letters of the word for hurried around

parts.note: ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A scoundrel rushed back in to spread gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' gives NAR, and 'in' puts it inside CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A false story or unfounded report, a hoax.

clue.text: Buy shares in clothing

parts.note: a vest is an item of clothing, an undershirt

explanation.surface: Purchasing stock in a clothes company.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting money into stocks to earn a return.

clue.text: Peg will not quite succeed

indicators.note: not quite says the phrase is cut short at its end

parts.note: to do well is to succeed

explanation.surface: A man called Peg will fall a little short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last L from DO WELL; 'will' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden pin used to join pieces of furniture.

clue.text: Potential earl went round small house in Pakistan

definitions.note: the definition points to a place found in that country, a city

indicators.note: went round places the anagram around the short house
potential means not yet in its final form, so the letters of earl are rearranged

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A would-be aristocrat circled a cottage in Pakistan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potential' rearranges EARL into LARE, and 'went round' puts it around HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A major city of Punjab province, the country's second largest.

clue.text: Humble cleric going round Middle East

indicators.note: going round puts the cleric's letters around the region

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric

explanation.surface: A modest churchman travelling round the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower or degrade someone's dignity, a verb sense.

clue.text: Elude trick

explanation.surface: Escaping by a ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade or avoid; and a cunning ruse or scheme.

clue.text: Make a priest or American attorney in the end

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: Becoming a clergyman or a prosecutor eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in order; 'the end' says IN closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To confer holy orders on someone, admitting them to the clergy.

clue.text: Desmond followed George' into the rock cavities

indicators.note: followed tells us Desmond's short form comes after George's

parts.note: Geo. is the abbreviation for George
Des is short for Desmond

explanation.surface: Two men walking into caves in the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollow stones lined with crystals, cavities in rock.

clue.text: Down where the kangaroos are

parts.note: Australia is known as Down ... ; the word completing the phrase is also a synonym of down

explanation.surface: Downstairs in the land of kangaroos.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath, below, and the second word of the nickname for Australia.

clue.text: They always meet in the middle of the ring

definitions.text: They always meet in the middle of the ring

parts.words: They always meet in the middle of the ring
parts.note: lines from a circle's edge to its centre always converge; the surface suggests boxers

explanation.surface: Boxers always meeting in the centre of the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines from a circle's centre to its circumference all meet at the centre.

clue.text: Let Head Office arrange accommodation

indicators.note: arrange tells us the letters of let are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Head office allows staff to book lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' turns LET into TEL, which follows HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A building offering rooms for travellers, a place to stay.

clue.text: Ruth's chopping up wood

indicators.note: chopping up means the letters of Ruth's are cut and rearranged

parts.note: the name with its possessive s supplies five letters

explanation.surface: Ruth is cutting timber.
explanation.walkthrough: A hurst is an old word for a wooded hill, seen in place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A grove or wooded rise, an archaic term for woodland.

clue.text: Grand bedroom I redesigned for new union members

indicators.note: redesigned says the letters of the words are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A grand bedroom redone for newly-weds.
explanation.definitionFit: The couple at a wedding are the two members of a marriage, a new union.

clue.text: Nine atoms exploded in the state

indicators.note: exploded means the letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Nine atoms detonated somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the upper Midwest, capital St Paul.
